h1: Siam River Resort Chaiyaphum — an in-town resort with a pool and easy parking, on a modest budget
intro: If you're in Chaiyaphum and want somewhere with a resort feel and a pool to cool off in, but still in town and easy to drive around from — Siam River Resort is a name that keeps coming up. It's a 3-star, 108-room resort on Bannakarn Road in the city centre, with an outdoor pool, a big car park, and the bus station just about 2 km away. Rates start at around ฿900/night. The trade-off is that it's an older resort that's been open a long time, and some rooms haven't been renovated, so condition varies room to room.

body.html: What sets Siam River Resort apart from the in-town tower hotels in Chaiyaphum is the resort feel and the outdoor pool. Buildings spread across a wide plot with gardens and sit-out areas, and the swimming pool is the thing guests mention most when they want to cool off. There's a separate children's pool too, so it works reasonably well for families with kids. The resort opened in 2005 and had a partial renovation in 2020.

Another thing self-drivers love is the large, free car park — easy parking, no jostling for a space, and you can unload right by your room. The location is on Bannakarn Road in the city centre, about 2 km from Chaiyaphum bus station, so you can drive into town for food or errands in a few minutes. It's quieter than being on the main highway, but still genuinely in town rather than out on the edge.

Room types run from Deluxe Twin and Deluxe Double with balconies up to Deluxe Garden rooms and a Suite with a King bed and a sofa bed. Guests often praise the spacious, clean rooms, the full set of amenities, and the friendly staff — the reception team in particular gets singled out for being helpful, with a quick check-in. Rooms come with air-con, a TV, a fridge and hot water.
"Roomy, clean, a pool to cool off in, parked right outside the room, and lovely staff — for just over a thousand baht it's good value for Chaiyaphum."

To be straight about it, the most common complaint in the reviews is how dated the resort feels. Some rooms haven't been renovated, with tired bathrooms and furnishings; a few reviews mention a shower with no curtain, just a half partition. Mattresses are on the firm side, and the air-con in some rooms blows straight onto the bed. If your room looks too worn on arrival, ask reception to move you right away.

A couple more things to set expectations: breakfast is simple — several reviews describe it as plain, sometimes served cold — and the in-room Wi-Fi is weak in spots, even though the lobby signal is strong. The pool is saltwater, and a few past reviews mention it being closed for maintenance, so check ahead if swimming is a priority. Staff speak limited English, though that's no issue for Thai travellers.

Overall, Siam River Resort scores 7.9 out of 10 on Trip.com from around 7 real reviews. It's a solid fit for self-drivers who want a resort feel, a pool and easy parking while staying in town, on a modest budget. Rates start around ฿900 and rise with the season and room type. If you can live with the dated resort and a plain breakfast, it offers good value for the price.

honestSummary: Siam River Resort is a solid pick for self-drivers who want a resort feel and a pool in central Chaiyaphum on a modest budget — roomy rooms, easy parking, and friendly staff. The trade-off is that it's an older resort, and with some rooms not yet renovated, condition isn't consistent room to room.
honestChecks: If you're particular about modern, renovated rooms — this is an older resort and some rooms haven't been updated → ask for a renovated room when booking, or consider the newer Park Villa Chaiyaphume.
If you're coming mainly to use the pool — a few past reviews mention it being closed for maintenance → call the hotel ahead to confirm the pool is open during your stay.
If firm mattresses or air-con blowing on you keep you up — some rooms have firm beds and the AC blows onto the bed → ask reception to switch rooms or adjust the air-con direction at check-in.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Siam River Resort Chaiyaphum

faq.q: Where is Siam River Resort in Chaiyaphum, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Siam River Resort is at 55 Bannakarn Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Chaiyaphum. It's a resort in the city centre, about 2 km (a 5-minute drive) from Chaiyaphum bus station, near the Chao Pho Phaya Lae Monument and the town market. You can drive into town in just a few minutes.

faq.q: How much does Siam River Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿900/night for a Deluxe Double. Choices run from Deluxe Twin and Deluxe Garden rooms up to a Suite with a King bed and a sofa bed. Prices rise with the season and room type — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Siam River Resort have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both. There's an outdoor saltwater swimming pool with a children's pool, and a large free car park where you can park near your room. The pool is a guest favourite, but a few past reviews mention it being closed for maintenance, so check ahead if swimming is a priority.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Siam River Resort — are they dated?
faq.a: Rooms are fairly spacious and clean with a full set of amenities, but the resort opened in 2005 and some rooms haven't been renovated, so condition varies. A few reviews mention old furnishings and bathrooms, and firm mattresses — ask for a renovated room when you book.

faq.q: Who is Siam River Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a good fit for self-drivers who want a resort feel and a pool in central Chaiyaphum on a modest budget, and for families with kids (there's a children's pool). If you want a more modern, updated room, consider the newer Park Villa Chaiyaphume instead.

faq.q: What is breakfast like at Siam River Resort?
faq.a: Breakfast is fairly simple — several reviews describe it as plain and sometimes served cold — and starts around 6:30. If you'd prefer something heartier, there are restaurants in town just a few minutes' drive away.
